Aggrieved by the Judgment passed by the 11 th ACMM, Mayohall Unit, in C.C.No.24603/2010,
dated.21.08.2021 by convicting the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec. 419 and 420 of IPC,
the Appellant has preferred this appeal.
2. For convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking in the trial court.

3. In brief, the case of the complainant/respondent is that on 13/1/2010 CW.1 Smt.Vijayalakshmi,

sentences.text:
On the basis of the complaint,case was registered in Cr.No.09/2010 and after investigation,
chargesheet has been filed.
5. After taking cognizance of the offence, summons was issued, in pursuance of summons, accused appeared before the trial court and released on bail.
After hearing both side, charge was framed and explained to the accused, for which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Thereafter the prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to 6, got marked 6 documents and two material object marked as M.O.1 and 2.
Thereafter, statement of the accused u/s 313 of Cr.P.C has been recorded.
Accused has denied all the incriminating evidence against him.
After hearing arguments of both side, the trial court has passed the impugned judgment dt: 21.08.2021, convicting the accused for the alleged offence.

Being aggrieved by the said impugned judgment , the appellant/accused has preferred this appeal on the following:
Crl.A.No.25145/2021 GROUNDS 1.
The judgment of the Trial Court is illegal, capricious and contrary to law and facts.
2. The trial court has passed the judgment without appreciating the evidence and documents.

3. The impugned judgment passed by the trial court is unsustainable in law, hence,
interference of this court is necessary.

6. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for appellant and Learned P.P. and perused the records.
7.

The points that arisen for consideration of this court are as under:-
1. Whether the appeal preferred by the appellant is deserves to be allowed?
2. Whether the impugned Judgment dtd.21.08.2021 passed by the trial court is not just and proper and needs interference of this court?
3. What order?

2 8. The findings of this court on the above points are as under:-
Point No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : In the Negative, Point No.3 : As per the final order for the following:
REASONS 9. Point No.1 and 2 :- These two points are interconnected, they are taken together for consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

10. To substantiate the case, the prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to 6, got marked documents at Ex.P1 to 6 and two material objects as M.O.1 and 2.
11.
PW.1 is the complainant.

In her evidence she deposed regarding discharge of her duties as a Asst.Traffic Inspector and while discharging her duty along with Cws.2 and 3 on 13.1.2010 at about 11-00am, in a bus bearing No.4342 accused travelled from 'Nagawara' bus stop to 'Indian Express'
bus stop with a pass bearing No.038525 and on enquiry it was found that said pass is Crl.A.No.25145/2021 created one.
Hence, she lodged a complaint before the Police as per Ex.P1.
Though sufficient opportunity was given, accused did not choose to cross-examine PW.1.

Hence,
cross-examination of PW.1 was taken as Nil.
Thereafter, accused filed application for recalling of PW.1 for cross-examination, it was came to be allowed by trial court and summons was issued to PW.1.
After issuance of summons, PW.1 not tendered herself to undergo cross- examination by accused.
Then the trial court discarded the evidence of PW.1.
But, the trial court ought not to have discarded the evidence of PW.1 as accused himself has obtained adjournment for cross-examination when PW.1 was present.
12. Though the evidence of PW.1 is discarded by the trial court, it is not fatal to the case of the prosecution.

The remaining witnesses who are examined before the trial curt as PW.2, 3 and 6 are supported the case of the prosecution and the evidence of PW.2, 3 and 6 Crl.A.No.25145/2021 substantiated the case of the prosecution.
Though sufficient time was given, PW.2, 3 and 5 were not cross- examined by the accused.
PW.4 and 6 though cross- examined, nothing has been elicited from their mouth in support of the accused.
13. PW.4 is the pass issuing authority has deposed before the trial court that he has not issued pass as per Ex.P. 5.
He submitted his report as per Ex.P. 4 and he deposed that Ex.P. 5 pass is forged by accused.
14. PW.5 is the Investigation Officer.
The evidence of PW.5 also discloses with respect to commission of crime by the accused.

On the basis of the evidence of PW.2,3,4, 5 and 6, the trial court has convicted the accused for the offences punishable u/s 419 and 420 of IPC by holding that prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence, for the aforesaid reasons, the trial court has rightly convicted the accused assigning proper and just reasons.

Hence,
there is no need of Crl.A.No.25145/2021 interference of this court.
Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, the appeal preferred by the appellant is not deserves to be allowed.

Therefore, this court Mohammed Wasim vs Pulakeshinagar Ps on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12791191/
3 answers Points No.1 and 2 in the Negative.

15. Point No.3:-In view of the findings and reasons given to point No.1 and 2, this court proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Criminal Appeal No. 25145/2021 filed by the Appellant/ Accused u/S.374(3) of Cr.P.C. is dismissed.

The Judgment passed by XI ACMM.,
 Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru in  C.C.No.24603/2010 dtd. 21.08.2010 is  confirmed.
